FDA Approves First DNA Medicine to Reduce Repeat Airway Surgeries

byDeepti Shroff, DMD, MS
November 10, 2026
in Infectious Disease, Pharma, Pulmonology, Surgery
Reading Time: 2 mins read
Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedIn
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:45
Instaread
1. The FDA granted Voceryq accelerated approval for the treatment of recurrent respiratory papillomatosis.
2. Among patients using Voceryq in a clinical study, 27% required no surgeries in the first year after treatment. 
On October 30th, the FDA published a report that Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) received accelerated approval for the treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP). This rare, human papillomavirus (HPV) driven disease leads to the formation of growths in patient airways. Approximately 25,000 people in the United States currently have RRP. This groundbreaking therapy marks the first plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy in the United States. It offers a treatment option for patients which actually targets the root cause of the disease, utilizes the patient’s own immune system to fight against it, and reduces the need for multiple surgical interventions. A trial evaluating the clinical efficacy and safety of Voceryq included 32 adults with RRP who had at least two surgeries to remove growths related to RRP in the past year before starting Voceryq treatment. The results of the study found that 27% of patients who had three baseline surgeries did not require any surgeries for the first full year following treatment. The most common side effects noted included injection site pain and/or adverse reactions, headache, fatigue, high blood pressure, nausea, and dizziness. A confirmatory trial to further describe the clinical benefit of Voceryq is expected to be conducted by Inovio Pharmaceuticals by the end of this year.
Further reading: FDA News
